description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 (relayed by JSON: "yes. cheap try."; earlier: "that just points to our try mechanism being a little stupid, forcing us into further stupidity"). Proposal page first.

Measured (JSON session, AOT build): a loop of 18 digits per number over 1M numbers, with and without `try do ... rescue _ -> 0 end`: instructions 2.758-2.760G -> 3.120-3.122G over three runs each, ~362 instructions per try that never raises. Per 1000 iterations native run continuation_allocs 1010 -> 3011: a try adds 2 heap continuations of 96 B each. The interpreter allocates nothing for either loop. Probes: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/ebbfffd8-2561-4da7-bcda-f9a316d00a1e/scratchpad/ovf/ (plain.fz, try.fz for instructions; tk.fz for allocation kinds). BEAM: entering a try pushes a catch tag on the stack, a couple of instructions.

Why: a try this expensive pushes library code away from idiomatic error handling (lib/json.fz carries `integer | :overflow` per digit, re-checking overflow that * and + already raise; up to 2.6% of distiller cycles).

The page answers where the two continuations come from in native try lowering and what an unraised try should cost. The exceptions epic fz-3ul is closed; Bugs and Cleanup last built that code (fz-3sy.34/.35).

comments.text: Probe sources copied to /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-9x7.31-probes/ (plain.fz and try.fz for instructions, tk.fz for allocation kinds; the other .fz files came from the same scratch directory). Page author: Bugs and Cleanup, starting after fz-sc8.246 has a PR; starts from measurements.

title: An unraised try allocates nothing and costs almost nothing
